question: Holding each output/purpose and implementation fixed, how does input/effects wording influence finite-equivalence retrieval?
scope: Eight previously exposed synthetic development functions; not new independent cases

A.effects: Pure calculation without allocation or external state.

B.input: An integer value in the inclusive interval 0 to 255.
B.effects: No allocation and no externally visible state changes; only a return value.

intervention: Replace input and effects only; purpose/output stay byte-identical. Fixed block-size behavior remains in purpose/output; this is wording of common domain/effects, not all prose style.
assignments: All 256 binary assignments to sorted eight IDs, no selected best assignment
fit: Each representation fits union of A and B versions before scoring; transductive controlled vocabulary. Fields fit separately for field_mean; equal four-field weights.
ranking: Descending positive cosine rounded to 12 decimals; lexical unordered pair breaks ties; top3
measurements: Distribution of finite-equivalent hits@3; for each fixed pair mean same-style minus different-style similarity; whole ranking and all pairs retained
negative_control: output_only scores and rankings must be identical across assignments
limits: Exact finite behavior labels replayed from prior traces; no refactoring benefit or shared-mechanism negatives. Two-field wording intervention, not general stylistic causality. No code baseline rerun or parameter tuning.
